statusText: The CME weekend halt still governs the assessment: no venue has quoted NQ since Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and none will until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, about thirteen hours beyond the end of this 24-hour horizon. Tail therefore holds at 10% (low), keeping the action EA_ON and the status green - a pathological one-way price path cannot form while nothing is quoting, and the low non-zero level prices weekend headline discontinuity rather than observed extension. For the second consecutive hour the wires did move, and on a front that had not been active in this weekend's assessments. The Houthis fired six ballistic missiles at the Red Sea port of Mokha at roughly 08:45 UTC, killing a security guard, wounding eight and leaving two marines missing; and Lebanese media reported a fresh IDF strike at Deir al-Zahrani, north of Nabatieh, at roughly 09:14 UTC - a third distinct Lebanese target set today after Ansar and the Ali Taher Ridge. The Mokha barrage is a continuation of a Houthi tempo running since roughly 10 August rather than a brand-new front, which is why it is scored as an increment rather than a step change. Both items are escalatory in direction and neither is observable in price, so both go where the contract puts them - Stress, which lifts one point to 51% (elevated), not Tail. Confidence stays at 59% (medium-low): every obtainable input was re-verified from primary sources this hour, but a weekend futures halt with no live price path is precisely the case the contract reserves that band for.
recommendation: Action is EA_ON with a green status, derived from current Tail (10%) alone. No venue quotes NQ anywhere in the 24-hour horizon and no scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside it, so there is no basis for a directional or event-driven block in this window; existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The operative checkpoint sits just beyond the horizon at the CME reopen near 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, and the danger window brackets that reopen together with its first 90 minutes of price discovery - a full weekend of accumulated headlines expresses there as an opening gap, not as intraday structure. Gap risk is genuinely two-way. Pulling one way: a Hormuz closure Tehran says will not lift until its conditions are met, a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports still in force, repeated attacks on ADNOC vessels including a third in one week, Bessent's threatened economic isolation with measures due next week, a Lebanon exchange that has now produced three separate target sets in a single day, a Houthi missile campaign against Mokha that keeps a second maritime chokepoint in play, and Tehran publicly disowning the negotiation track. Pulling the other: the Iran-Oman talks on defining a sea route through the Strait are still running, Tehran continues to frame reopening as conditional rather than impossible, and Friday's equity tape absorbed two sharp consumer misses with rotation rather than directional selling. Crude can reprice before equities are able to, and the soft consumer picture leaves a second, unrelated growth-scare channel open into the 19 August FOMC minutes. This is a general market-risk assessment for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice, and no trade is being placed or recommended.
headline: A second hour of new escalation with no tape to price it - six Houthi ballistic missiles hit Mokha and a third IDF strike lands at Deir al-Zahrani - but with the CME shut until Sunday night Tail holds at 10% on EA_ON while Stress firms to 51%.
body:
PRICE PATH (observed, stale by necessity). No venue has quoted NQ since the CME weekly close at 21:00 UTC on Friday 14 August, and none will until the Sunday reopen near 22:00 UTC on 16 August. The last live structure, re-verified this hour from primary sources, remains benign: September E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures show a last print of 30,141.75, -46.75 points or -0.15% against a previous close of 30,188.50, with the session settling mid-range inside a 30,028.50-30,283.00 band roughly 255 points or 0.84% wide, and no close near either extreme. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,046.14, -38.36 points or -0.13%, inside a 29,934.66-30,179.82 range and about 2.3% below the 52-week high of 30,762.20. A two-way intraday range with a mid-range settle is the opposite of the persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks and repeated extension that the Tail definition requires. Directional efficiency, pullback depth, failed-retracement counts and proximity to session extremes are all unobservable this hour; that is a structural absence of evidence, not evidence of calm, and it is the single reason Confidence stays medium-low.

CROSS-ASSET (observed, Friday close). VIX closed at 14.25, -0.38 or -2.60%, in a 14.18-14.72 day range and near the bottom of its 13.38-35.30 52-week band - the options market priced no stress into the weekend. The latest H.15 constant-maturity yields, for 13 August, are 2Y 4.15%, 10Y 4.63% and 30Y 5.21%: a positively sloped curve with no acute front-end repricing, and no update is due before Monday. Crude is the one asset carrying the geopolitical premium and it is carrying it clearly - WTI $82.40, +$1.15 or +1.42% on the day, more than +5% on the week, +3.52% on the month and roughly +33% year-over-year, with Brent at $88.52, +$1.45 or +1.67%. This remains a textbook conflicting-signal set: equity volatility asleep, rates orderly, energy repricing a supply shock. Per the risk definitions, conflicting signals belong in Stress, not Tail, and that is where they are scored.

GEOPOLITICS (new escalation on a second maritime front, still unpriceable). This hour produced two new timestamped items. First, Yemen. The Houthis fired six ballistic missiles at the Red Sea port of Mokha at roughly 08:45 UTC; one security guard was killed, eight were wounded and two marines are missing. Cross-checking that against reporting from Al Arabiya, France 24 and Al Jazeera shows a sustained campaign against Mokha and its commercial port running since roughly 10 August, with earlier barrages killing between four and seven people - so this is an intensification of an existing tempo rather than the opening of a new front, and it is scored as an increment. It matters for the index only through the energy and shipping channel, keeping a second maritime chokepoint in play alongside Hormuz. Second, Lebanon. Lebanese media reported a fresh IDF strike at Deir al-Zahrani, north of Nabatieh, at roughly 09:14 UTC. That is a third distinct target set today after the Ansar strike, which killed seven and wounded three, and the heavy strikes on the Ali Taher Ridge, both of which the IDF confirmed at roughly 08:08 UTC were carried out in response to a Hezbollah attack on its forces. A single confirmed retaliatory exchange has become a running sequence across a day. Everything else is unchanged and unresolved: the Persian Gulf Strait Authority maintains the Strait 'remains blocked and will not be reopened until Iran's conditions are accepted'; Araghchi said at roughly 05:09 UTC that Tehran has not decided to resume talks with Washington, that messages passing through Qatar and Pakistan do not amount to negotiations, and that Washington must meet conditions before shipping resumes, while the separate Oman track on defining a sea route continues; the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports stands; Bessent's threatened economic isolation, with measures due next week, still sits ahead; and the Hormuz vessel attacks reported at roughly 07:22 UTC - an ADNOC tanker and a bulk carrier struck by an unknown projectile - are now framed by the wires as the third ADNOC vessel hit in a single week. Transits through the Strait remain a small fraction of the roughly 130 a day seen before the war, and the IEA has cut its second-half 2026 global demand estimate by about 550 kb/d on the closure.

MACRO (observed). Friday's U.S. consumer prints both missed sharply: Retail Sales -0.6% month-over-month against +0.1% consensus, Retail Sales ex-autos -0.3% against +0.2%, and preliminary August Michigan sentiment 51.0 against 54.5. Equities absorbed those misses with two-way volatility and rotation rather than directional efficiency - the reason Tail sat at 7-9% through that cash session while Stress built into the low 40s. The soft-consumer channel is a second, independent thread into the 19 August FOMC minutes, unrelated to the Middle East. No U.S. macro release falls inside this 24-hour horizon; the calendar restarts with the NY Empire State survey at 12:30 UTC on Monday 17 August, and the FOMC minutes for the July 28-29 meeting are confirmed against the Federal Reserve's own August calendar for 18:00 UTC on Wednesday 19 August.

SCORING (inference). Tail 10% - low band, EA_ON, green. A shut venue cannot produce a pathological price path, and none of the amplifier conditions the contract requires for 25%+ is observable, let alone confirmed. The level is unchanged despite new escalation because the new information is headline flow with no venue to express it, and because the reopen at which it would express falls about thirteen hours beyond the end of this horizon. Stress 51% - elevated, up one point. Two items widened the picture this hour on primary-source evidence and neither is resolved, but the Mokha barrage extends a campaign already running for five days rather than opening something new, so the increment is one point rather than a step. Letting Stress decay while the Strait is blocked, a sanctions package is a week out and the Lebanon exchange is running across three target sets in a day would misstate the backdrop. Confidence 59% - medium-low. Every obtainable input was obtained and re-verified against primary sources this hour, and the new material was cross-checked before scoring - the Mokha attack was verified against three independent outlets to establish it as a continuation rather than a first strike. The remaining gap is structural, and a weekend futures halt with no live price path is precisely the case the contract reserves the medium-low band for. Dominant mode is mixed: a halted tape overlaid on genuinely conflicting cross-asset signals and two-way geopolitical threads.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 clock-hours Tail never left the low band, running 2-10% throughout. It held 9% through Friday's European session, eased to 7-9% across the U.S. cash session as the sharp Retail Sales and Michigan sentiment misses produced two-way volatility and rotation rather than directional efficiency, and printed 6% into the 21:00 UTC weekly close. Stress described a clear event arc: 27-38% in the Friday morning hours, building to 40-44% through the U.S. cash session as the data landed, then 34% at the close. The two runs immediately after the close scored the halt itself at Tail 2% and Stress 12%; from 00:00 UTC onward that reading was corrected back to Tail 9% and Stress 45% on the judgement that a shut venue does not neutralise a live Hormuz closure, and 45% then held for six consecutive hours through 05:00 UTC. The 06:00 and 07:00 UTC slots lifted to Tail 10% and Stress 48% on the overnight Ansar strike and the UAE's accusation over the ADNOC tanker attacks, and the 08:00 slot took Stress to 50% when the IDF confirmed the Lebanon exchange was retaliatory and Araghchi disowned the U.S. talks track. Those past opinions are preserved exactly as published and have not been rewritten in light of the Mokha barrage or the Deir al-Zahrani strike confirmed this hour. Confidence spent the Friday session in the 30s-50s and firmed to 56-59% after midnight as primary-source verification improved. One slot, 20:00 UTC on 14 August, has no published Claude assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt - it runs from 09:00 UTC on Saturday 15 August to 08:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, ending roughly thirteen hours before the reopen near 22:00 UTC that day - so neither a scheduled U.S. macro release nor a tradable price path falls within it. Tail is projected flat at 10% for the first eleven slots and ticking to 11% from 20:00 UTC on 15 August as the reopen edges into view; that increment reflects accumulating gap risk, not observed structure, and every slot stays deep in the low band, so the action is EA_ON and the status green throughout. Stress is projected to hold at 51% through the European afternoon, ease a single point to 50% across the thin Saturday U.S. hours when weekend headline flow is historically lightest, then firm back to 51% into the late slots and 52% through Sunday's European morning as unresolved threads converge on the reopen: the Hormuz impasse and Tehran's conditions of sanctions relief, asset unfreezing and an end to the Lebanon and Gaza wars; the standing U.S. naval blockade and the sanctions package Bessent has promised for next week; a Lebanon exchange that has produced three target sets in a single day; an intensifying Houthi campaign against Mokha that keeps a second maritime chokepoint in play; Araghchi's statement that Tehran has not decided to resume talks, set against the still-running Oman routing track; and a soft U.S. consumer picture heading into the 19 August FOMC minutes. Confidence drifts down within the medium-low band from 59% to 56% purely as the last live print recedes further into the past. The real checkpoint sits just beyond this horizon: the reopen at roughly 22:00 UTC on 16 August, which the danger window brackets together with its first 90 minutes of trade. Gap risk there is two-way, and the first live tape - not this forecast - is what will decide whether Tail leaves the low band.

forecastDetail.comment: Current hour. European Saturday late morning, the third full day of the CME weekend halt, and the second consecutive hour in which new escalation printed with no venue able to express it. Since the last assessment the Houthis fired six ballistic missiles at the Red Sea port of Mokha at roughly 08:45 UTC, killing a security guard, wounding eight and leaving two marines missing, and Lebanese media reported a fresh IDF strike at Deir al-Zahrani north of Nabatieh at roughly 09:14 UTC - a third distinct target set in Lebanon today. Tail holds at 10% because no venue quotes NQ, so directional efficiency, pullback depth and proximity to extremes stay unobservable; the new material lifts Stress a point to 51%.

Saturday midday. Weekend headline flow historically thins from here into the European afternoon, and no scheduled U.S. macro release exists anywhere in this horizon. Tail unchanged at 10% - a halted tape cannot generate the persistent directional efficiency the definition requires - with Stress held at 51% because the Hormuz closure, the U.S. naval blockade, the promised sanctions package and the now three-location Lebanon exchange are all still unresolved rather than decaying.

Early European Saturday afternoon. Expect verification rather than new information: the value of these hours is confirming whether the Mokha barrage and the Deir al-Zahrani strike are isolated or the start of a sustained weekend tempo. Tail flat at 10%, Stress flat at 51%, confidence steady at the top of the medium-low band.

Saturday afternoon, the U.S. would-be cash window with no cash market. Both instruments remain unquotable, so the assessment is entirely a carry-forward of Friday's benign closing structure plus live headline risk. Tail 10%, Stress 51%.

Saturday U.S. morning hours. Statistically the quietest stretch of the weekend for both official statements and wire coverage; Stress eases a single point to 50% to reflect that thinner flow, not any resolution of the underlying threads. Tail unchanged at 10% and the action stays EA_ON.

Saturday early U.S. afternoon. Still no tape, no scheduled release and roughly thirty-two hours until the CME reopens near 22:00 UTC on Sunday. Tail 10%, Stress 50%; the first live print after the reopen, not this forecast, is what decides whether Tail leaves the low band.
